events.headline: Iran-linked attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz accelerated through early November 2026 (at least 8 vessels struck since Nov 1, including a VLCC engine-room strike and a tanker fire forcing a 25-person evacuation), with the US and Iran trading strikes on vessels over the Nov 7-8 weekend despite a fragile truce; JMIC data shows ~490 vessels queued outside the strait and Kpler puts flows at ~68% of the pre-war 17.1M bpd baseline

China's Ministry of Commerce extended (announced Nov 9) its suspension of expanded October-2025 export controls on rare earths, lithium-battery materials and graphite anodes by roughly two months rather than letting it lapse on the original Nov 10 deadline, easing near-term supply-chain disruption risk for materials buyers; note heavier April-2025 licensing rules on elements like dysprosium/terbium/yttrium remain in force

US October CPI (released Nov 10) ran hot for a third straight month — headline +0.4% m/m vs +0.3% consensus, core +0.3% vs +0.2% — lifting priced odds of a Fed hike at the Dec 9 FOMC meeting (one market cited ~85.5% odds of a move) and prompting a Dallas Fed official to call for two more quarter-point increases

Nasdaq and S&P 500 surged on Nov 11 as chip and AI names rebounded sharply — CoreWeave paced a broad AI-infrastructure rally and Nvidia bounced back from its prior-week selloff — even as the hot CPI print above kept Fed-hike odds elevated

Nvidia's board-level independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's reported ties to an executive accused of passing information to Beijing remains open with no findings yet; three House committee chairs pressed Huang to accept a Nov 18 closed-door briefing date (or propose an alternative by Nov 11), keeping a governance overhang on AI/semis names ahead of Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings even as the stock rebounded
